title: Narcotic Treatment Pathways
rule_summary: Federal law distinguishes ordinary controlled-prescription practice from narcotic maintenance/detoxification treatment. Methadone OUD maintenance generally follows the narcotic-treatment-program framework. Under the narrow non-OTP emergency provision in 21 CFR 1306.07(b), a practitioner may dispense, but not prescribe, not more than a three-day supply of narcotic medication at one time while arrangements for referral are made; that emergency treatment may not be renewed or extended. Qualifying Schedule III-V narcotic treatment may use a prescription pathway when otherwise lawful.
exam_relevance: Tests a distinct pharmacist decision path using current official authority rather than rote trivia.

authority.name: DEA Diversion Control Division
authority.section: Instructions to request exception to 21 CFR 1306.07(b) 3-day rule

common_confusions: The current emergency limit is up to a three-day supply dispensed at one time; the former one-day-at-a-time language is obsolete. The pathway authorizes dispensing, not a routine retail prescription, and may not be renewed or extended.
verification_notes: Repaired after independent Batch 2 audit PR #36 / adjudication Issue #37 to reflect the current 21 CFR 1306.07(b) three-day-supply-at-one-time rule. Requires fresh independent re-audit before release.
